overall: The AG found the Reading Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law by untimely approving the April 14 and May 13 minutes and by requiring advance registration for the July 22 meeting; other allegations were declined or not violations.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged members communicated electronically with each other and with the public during the February 11 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Where the allegation that Board members improperly communicated during the February 11 meeting was discoverable more than 30 days before the June 18 complaint was filed, we find this allegation untimely and decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the February 11 minutes were insufficient for omitting members' electronic communications, including emails or texts viewed during the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the public body is not required to record the communication in its meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board improperly 'preapproved' the February 11 minutes at its May 13 meeting, subject to amendments.
allegations.key_passage: Because June 18 and July 27 are more than 30 days after the May 13 meeting, we find this allegation to be untimely as well.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board discussed adopting a summary, roughly two-page minute format that would violate the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation because it was not timely filed with the Board and because it does not allege a violation of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board repeatedly failed to approve and release minutes on time since January 2020, without identifying specific sets.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint does not identify any specific set of minutes, other than those of the April 14 and May 13 meetings, as being untimely approved, we decline to review the general allegation

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to timely approve the minutes of its April 14 and May 13 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges, and we find, that the Board violated the Law where it did not approve the minutes of the April 14 and May 13 meetings until well past the 30 day or three meeting timeframe allowed for under the regulations.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the July 22 retreat was not accessible because the public had to register in advance and was not recorded by local TV.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board’s July 22 meeting was not accessible to the public, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the July 22 retreat was improperly unrecorded by RCTV; the Board offered access only through Zoom.
allegations.key_passage: We find the Board did not violate the Law where it chose to allow public access to its July 22 meeting in real time via Zoom, and did not otherwise broadcast or record the meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no further remedial action ordered because the Board had already released draft minutes and edited documents from the July 22 meeting).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
